items.label: Applied Materials semicon west 2026 (10-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Demand framework: CEO said Applied saw significant growth in agentic

set.signal: Demand framework: CEO said Applied saw significant growth in agentic AI compute demand in calendar 2026 and has increased its wafer fab equipment forecast going forward because of it (no WFE number given); an agentic AI factory pod consumes about 2-4 times more wafers than a generative AI pod (Rubin and Rubin Ultra configurations), and 85% of the content of the agentic AI factory by wafer starts is leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM and advanced packaging; server CPU, GPU, networking and ASIC chips are moving to the leading edge faster. Semiconductor Products Group President Prabu Raja: Applied's SAM is around 55% of the WFE market, and around 75% of all WFE growth through 2030 is expected in leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM and advanced packaging, where Applied is number one; Applied raised several SAM numbers because more process steps (treatments, anneals, thermal interface materials) are being ordered.
set.figure: agentic AI pod about 2-4 times more wafers than a generative AI pod; 85% of agentic AI factory content; Applied SAM around 55% of WFE; around 75% of WFE growth through 2030 in three segments

items.reason: Removed the 'over 2 percentage points of WFE share by 2030' clause: the same target already sits in this label's guidance entry on the same node (one fact once). Rest verified.
items.evidence: Applied expects to gain over 2 percentage market points of WFE share by 2030.

items.label: Applied Materials semicon west 2026 (10-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Metrology and inspection (Keith Wells, head of the Imaging and Process

set.signal: Metrology and inspection (Keith Wells, head of the Imaging and Process Control Group): Applied expects '$3 billion in systems and service revenue in 2026' for M&I, with very high growth going forward. Optical inspection is a $9 billion market of which Applied serves only about $2 billion today; new optical products over the next few years target the $7 billion of additional TAM, where customers want alternatives to incumbents. In E-beam, cold field emission technology gave Applied 2X revenue over its nearest competitor; many new E-beam tools are planned over the next few years. A new on-device, in-line X-ray materials metrology capability (built on CFE) is now used at customers; Keith: 'we think that this new market ... is worth several hundred million dollars, and it's not in our P&L today.'
set.figure: M&I $3 billion systems and service revenue in 2026; optical inspection market $9 billion, Applied serves about $2 billion; $7 billion additional TAM; E-beam 2X revenue over nearest competitor; new X-ray metrology market several hundred million dollars

items.reason: Dropped 'optical and E-beam each +50% 2025 to 2026': restates the Goldman Sachs conference 2026 (09-09-2026) and Q3 FY2026 entries (eBeam and optical growing over 50% this calendar year); restored the 'we think' hedge on the X-ray market size.
items.evidence: So we think that this new market, which we're very excited about, is worth several hundred million dollars, and it's not in our P&L today.

items.label: Applied Materials semicon west 2026 (10-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Adjacent businesses (CEO): display and SENZ together run at around

set.signal: Adjacent businesses (CEO): display and SENZ together run at around $400 million per quarter and should not be modeled beyond that near term; display earns a little over 20% operating profit; MaxOLED, which eliminates the fine metal mask so OLED can move to IT, TV and automotive sizes, is being implemented with leading display companies as yields are brought to the high-volume tipping point; display deposition and E-beam leadership is being brought into semiconductor panel packaging. SENZ waveguides for AI glasses: around 90% of the flow is Applied custom innovation, and the strategy is to sell waveguides and eyepieces.
set.figure: around $400 million per quarter run rate; display a little over 20% operating profit; around 90% of waveguide flow Applied custom

items.evidence: We expect those businesses to be more than $2 billion by 2030.

items.label: Applied Materials semicon west 2026 (10-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Advanced packaging (Prabu Raja): Applied's advanced packaging business

set.signal: Advanced packaging (Prabu Raja): 'our advanced packaging is now expected to grow more than $5 billion within a few years', and Applied expects to outgrow the market over the next 5 years as its on-chip wiring technologies move to chip-to-chip wiring (micro bumps, bumps, TSVs). In hybrid bonding Applied's portfolio addresses 80% of the steps across pre-bonding, bonding and post-bonding, partnering with Besi for the die-to-wafer bonding step (Kinex integrated tool); hybrid bonding is already adopted in HBM, 3D IC logic and co-packaged optics. For the silicon-interposer-to-panel transition Applied has built a panel portfolio, organic and inorganic, including acquisitions of Tango, a panel PVD company and NEXX (panel copper plating); Applied also acquired Sigray for X-ray.
set.figure: advanced packaging 'expected to grow more than $5 billion within a few years'; hybrid bonding portfolio addresses 80% of the steps

items.reason: The speaker said 'grow more than $5 billion', not 'grow to more than $5 billion' - quoted verbatim instead of interpreting; Sigray was named as an X-ray acquisition, not part of the panel portfolio.
items.evidence: Because of this, our advanced packaging is now expected to grow more than $5 billion within a few years, and we expect to outgrow the market in next 5 years.

items.label: Applied Materials semicon west 2026 (10-13-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Packaging inspection (Keith Wells): the optical inspection market

set.signal: Packaging inspection (Keith Wells): the optical inspection market for advanced packaging went from a few hundred million a couple of years ago to well over $1 billion as customers inspect every die before placement; Applied started a completely new, cost-effective optical inspection platform for it after about a year and a half studying the market - Keith: 'we feel that we're going to bring something to market that is clearly differentiated', positioned to have 'the highest sensitivity at the highest throughput possible'. Applied's front-end E-beam products adapted for back-end packaging are already generating revenue across multiple products, and Applied is 'starting to see an inflection where our customers are willing to accept higher ASPs' to meet packaging yield demands.
set.figure: advanced packaging optical inspection market from a few hundred million to well over $1 billion

items.reason: Restored the speaker's hedges: the differentiation is 'we feel', the spec is a positioning aim ('trying to position'), and the ASP point is 'starting to see an inflection', not a stated fact.
items.evidence: We are trying to position the product to have the highest sensitivity at the highest throughput possible ... we're starting to see an inflection where our customers are willing to accept higher ASPs
